nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n_1}$ and $c = (c_j)_{j \in n_2}$ be bases of $V$ indexed by finite types $n_1$ and $n_2$. Then the rank of $B$ with respect to $b$ equals the rank of the Gram matrix $(B(c_i, c_j))_{i, j \in n_2}$ of $B$ in $c$.
nodes.title: Basis independence of the rank of a bilinear form

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n}$ be a basis of $V$ indexed by a finite type $n$. Then the rank of $B$ with respect to $b$ equals the rank of the Gram matrix $(B(b_i, b_j))_{i, j \in n}$. This holds by definition.
nodes.title: Rank of a bilinear form via its Gram matrix

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n}$ be a basis of $V$ indexed by a finite type $n$. The rank of $B$ with respect to $b$ is the rank of the Gram matrix $(B(b_i, b_j))_{i, j \in n}$ of $B$ in $b$.
nodes.title: Rank of a bilinear form

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n_1}$ and $c = (c_j)_{j \in n_2}$ be bases of $V$ indexed by finite types $n_1$ and $n_2$. Then the Gram matrices $(B(b_i, b_j))_{i, j \in n_1}$ and $(B(c_i, c_j))_{i, j \in n_2}$ have the same rank.
nodes.title: The Gram matrices of a bilinear form in two bases have the same rank

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
